content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "Using 10-K segment and MD&A disclosures on major customers (SFAS 131), compute the fraction of revenue attributable to the largest single customer. Rank firms cross-sectionally; use the trailing fiscal year. Combine with revenue volatility (std of YoY quarterly sales growth over 8 quarters) into a composite z-score.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and bargaining-power disadvantages; investors underprice this fragility, so it commands a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high customer-concentration firms"}, {"name": "Inventory-Sales Divergence", "construction": "Compute YoY growth in inventory (Compustat INVT) minus YoY growth in sales (SALE), measured at the most recent fiscal quarter. Rank cross-sectionally each month using the latest available quarterly data.", "rationale": "Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns/write-offs that the market is slow to incorporate.", "higher_returns_for": "low inventory-minus-sales growth (inventory lean relative to sales)"}, {"name": "Accrual Reversal Acceleration", "construction": "For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, from balance sheet) for the two most recent fiscal years; take the second difference (this year's accruals minus last year's accruals). Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Beyond the level of accruals, the acceleration of accruals captures the point at which earnings quality is deteriorating fastest, predicting sharper future earnings disappointments.", "higher_returns_for": "low accrual acceleration"}, {"name": "Capex Burst Relative to History", "construction": "Compute current-year capital expenditure (CAPX) divided by the average CAPX over the prior three years. Rank firms cross-sectionally at fiscal year-end.", "rationale": "Sudden capital-spending bursts reflect empire-building and overinvestment that erode future returns on capital, which investors extrapolate too optimistically.", "higher_returns_for": "low capex-burst ratio"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Persistence Score", "construction": "Flag firms that initiated a cash dividend within the last 4 quarters (from CRSP distribution codes) and scale by the payout as a fraction of trailing free cash flow (OANCF minus CAPX). Rank the continuous payout-coverage measure among initiators.", "rationale": "Dividend initiations backed by ample free-cash-flow coverage signal credible, sustainable profitability improvements that the market underreacts to.", "higher_returns_for": "high free-cash-flow-covered initiators"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum", "construction": "Using disclosed order backlog (Compustat OB) scaled by total assets, compute the YoY change. Rank firms cross-sectionally at fiscal year-end; restrict to firms that report backlog.", "rationale": "Rising backlog is a leading indicator of future revenue that is not yet in reported earnings, and analysts underweight this soft-order information.", "higher_returns_for": "high increase in scaled backlog"}, {"name": "R&D Reversal Post-Cut", "construction": "Compute YoY change in R&D expense (XRD) scaled by sales for the most recent fiscal year. Rank firms; focus on firms cutting R&D (negative change).", "rationale": "Cutting R&D to hit near-term earnings targets sacrifices future growth and signals managerial short-termism, leading to lower long-run returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high (increasing or stable) R&D-to-sales change"}, {"name": "Geographic Revenue Dispersion", "construction": "From segment geographic disclosures (SFAS 131), compute a Herfindahl index across geographic revenue segments (sum of squared revenue shares). Rank cross-sectionally; higher index = more geographically concentrated.", "rationale": "Geographically concentrated firms carry undiversified macro and regulatory exposure that investors underprice, earning a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high geographic concentration"}, {"name": "Selling Expense Efficiency Trend", "construction": "Compute SG&A (XSGA) divided by sales for the current and prior fiscal year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally, favoring firms whose SG&A-to-sales ratio is declining.", "rationale": "Improving operating efficiency (falling SG&A intensity) reflects durable margin expansion that the market recognizes only gradually.", "higher_returns_for": "firms with declining SG&A-to-sales"}, {"name": "Short-Term Debt Rollover Pressure", "construction": "Compute debt in current liabilities (DLC) divided by total debt (DLC + DLTT) at fiscal year-end. Rank firms cross-sectionally; higher ratio = greater near-term rollover need.", "rationale": "High reliance on short-maturity debt exposes firms to refinancing and rollover risk in tightening credit conditions, commanding a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high short-term-debt share"}]}
